source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS01 is one of Virginia's largest disclosed data centers at 114 MW, but its power source and grid connection are not published.

The facility reports 114 MW of IT capacity across 685,000 square feet in Sterling, Virginia. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that capacity implies roughly 2,850 racks. The operator does not disclose workload mix or actual tenant configuration, so the figure describes the building's ceiling rather than its use.

Among the 25 Virginia facilities that publish megawatt figures, this campus ranks third. Those 25 total 1,603 MW, making Ashburn AS01 about 7.1 percent of the state's disclosed IT load. Virginia has 330 mapped facilities, so the ones publishing capacity are a small minority. Most of the state's data center infrastructure is not open to public review at this level of detail.

For AI scaling, the disclosed number is the least interesting part. A campus of this size matters only if power reaches it. The data does not say whether the 114 MW comes from existing utility supply or new generation, where the grid connection point is, or whether the full capacity is allocated or available. LEED certification speaks to building efficiency, not to power source or grid characteristics. Without those facts, this facility's role in Virginia's power constraint cannot be assessed from the record.
